note: Owner 2026-10-26 21:37 (GSD re-entry per session): five sessions share one worktree with a flat .planning/STATE.md, workstreams workstream-a and workstream-b and a .phase-loop-run file. measure --compact prints a GSD line only for the sessions whose own transcript shows GSD work (typed GSD commands, GSD Skill calls, gsd-tools runs that read or change planning state, state-file writes), each with its own workstream, and an Active driver line only for a real loop skill the session invoked (the shipped list, the driver_skills setting, or a skill chained into a typed GSD command); a GSD-only session gets a passive GSD re-entry line instead. A session that only talked about GSD, searched for it, quoted it, read its files, wrote another file into a workstream folder, ran GSD maintenance or invoked a one-shot skill with --ws gets neither. The shared .planning/active-workstream pointer changes nothing. Also: /clear forgets what came before; rows a fork carried over count; the newest named workstream whose folder exists wins (a prose trailing dot dropped, also in the re-enter command); a GSD root in another checkout adds --cwd; the GSD lines come right after the git header so the 3,000 B cap cuts porcelain lines first; checkpoint --measured, the classic SessionStart(compact) block ([driver] line only beside an Active driver), begin's gsd object and the stage's gsd_state follow the same per-session facts
